title: Ras to ERK: Three Kinases in Series

scenes.visual: Dark-navy 16:9 canvas with one vertical cell cross-section filling 75% of frame height: warm slate-amber plasma membrane strip across the top, deep cytosol in the middle, soft indigo nuclear arc at the bottom. A gold growth-factor sphere drifts slowly toward a gold receptor spanning the membrane. Bold white title (size 40): 'Ras to ERK: Three Kinases in Series'.

scenes.tts: A growth factor stays outside the cell. Why does it take three kinases in a row to tell the nucleus? The receptor sits at the surface, yet the cell's genes lie deep inside. Carrying that order across the cytoplasm takes a carefully built relay.
scenes.caption: A growth factor stays outside the cell. Why does it take three kinases in a row to tell the nucleus? The receptor sits at the surface, yet the cell's genes lie deep inside. Carrying that order across the cytoplasm takes a carefully built relay.
scenes.visual: Keep the cell cross-section. The gold growth factor docks on the gold receptor, lighting up its cytoplasmic tail. A dotted glowing path traces downward from the membrane across the cytosol to DNA bars inside the indigo nucleus while three empty numbered slots (1, 2, 3) pulse gently in the cytosol.
scenes.narration: A growth factor stays outside the cell. Why does it take three kinases in a row to tell the nucleus? The receptor sits at the surface, yet the cell's genes lie deep inside. Carrying that order across the cytoplasm takes a carefully built relay.

scenes.tts: First, the active receptor recruits G R B two and S O S to the membrane. S O S makes membrane-anchored Ras drop G D P, so plentiful G T P binds instead. Ras is not a kinase. Bound G T P pulls two flexible switch loops taut, making a surface Raf can grip.
scenes.caption: First, the active receptor recruits Grb2 and SOS to the membrane. SOS makes membrane-anchored Ras drop GDP, so plentiful GTP binds instead. Ras is not a kinase. Bound GTP pulls two flexible switch loops taut, making a surface Raf can grip.
scenes.visual: Teal blocks labelled 'Grb2' and 'SOS' dock on the glowing gold receptor tail. Beside them, a dim coral block labelled 'Ras' anchored to the membrane inner face ejects a grey 'GDP' tag and catches a bright gold 'GTP' tag. Ras brightens to glowing coral-red as two curved surface arcs ('Switch loops') snap taut into a crisp notch. Empathy fix: Label the two loops 'Switch loops' as they snap taut.
scenes.narration: First, the active receptor recruits Grb2 and SOS to the membrane. SOS makes membrane-anchored Ras drop GDP, so plentiful GTP binds instead. Ras is not a kinase. Bound GTP pulls two flexible switch loops taut, making a surface Raf can grip.

scenes.tts: Active Ras acts by contact. It catches folded, resting Raf from the cytosol and holds Raf at the membrane. Binding alone does not open Raf. Contact with membrane lipids and further steps help it unfold. Two Raf kinase domains then pair side to side, which normal activation requires.
scenes.caption: Active Ras acts by contact. It catches folded, resting Raf from the cytosol and holds Raf at the membrane. Binding alone does not open Raf. Contact with membrane lipids and further steps help it unfold. Two Raf kinase domains then pair side to side, which normal activation requires.
scenes.visual: A folded emerald block labelled 'Raf' drifts up from the cytosol and latches onto glowing coral-red Ras-GTP's taut notch. As Raf touches the amber membrane underside, its hinged flap swings open. A second Ras-GTP recruits a second open emerald Raf; the two Raf kinase blocks slide together side to side and glow bright emerald ('Paired Raf').
scenes.narration: Active Ras acts by contact. It catches folded, resting Raf from the cytosol and holds Raf at the membrane. Binding alone does not open Raf. Contact with membrane lipids and further steps help it unfold. Two Raf kinase domains then pair side to side, which normal activation requires.

scenes.tts: Paired Raf phosphorylates the middle kinase, Mek, on two serines. Mek is unusual among protein kinases. Most kinases target either serine and threonine, or tyrosine alone. Mek is a dual-specificity kinase. It tags Erk on a threonine and a tyrosine, one residue apart, creating a two-phosphate lock.
scenes.caption: Paired Raf phosphorylates the middle kinase, MEK, on two serines. MEK is unusual among protein kinases. Most kinases target either serine and threonine, or tyrosine alone. MEK is a dual-specificity kinase. It tags ERK on a threonine and a tyrosine, one residue apart, creating a two-phosphate lock.
scenes.visual: Bright emerald paired Raf stamps two yellow-gold 'P' circles onto an electric-blue block labelled 'MEK' (labelled 'Ser, Ser'), turning MEK bright. Active blue MEK moves to a vivid violet block labelled 'ERK' and stamps two yellow-gold 'P' circles side by side on a protruding loop labelled 'Thr' and 'Tyr'; ERK lights up vividly.
scenes.narration: Paired Raf phosphorylates the middle kinase, MEK, on two serines. MEK is unusual among protein kinases. Most kinases target either serine and threonine, or tyrosine alone. MEK is a dual-specificity kinase. It tags ERK on a threonine and a tyrosine, one residue apart, creating a two-phosphate lock.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. Suppose a phosphatase removes just one of Erk's two phosphates, leaving the other phosphate attached. Does Erk stay half-active, or shut off completely?
scenes.caption: Pause and predict. Suppose a phosphatase removes just one of ERK's two phosphates, leaving the other phosphate attached. Does ERK stay half-active, or shut off completely?
scenes.visual: Zoom slightly on the glowing violet ERK block carrying both yellow-gold 'P' tags ('Thr-P', 'Tyr-P'). A crimson crescent labelled 'Phosphatase' drifts up beside the 'Tyr-P' tag. Question banner appears cleanly at top (size 30): 'One phosphate removed: half-active or off?'.
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. Suppose a phosphatase removes just one of ERK's two phosphates, leaving the other phosphate attached. Does ERK stay half-active, or shut off completely?

scenes.visual: Hold the question banner 'One phosphate removed: half-active or off?' on screen while the crimson phosphatase slowly pulses beside ERK's 'Tyr-P' tag and a subtle progress arc sweeps across the bottom corner.

scenes.tts: Erk shuts off completely. Removing either phosphate silences it, because Erk requires both to align its active site. In the test tube, if one hit has chance p, two independent hits have chance p squared. So one in ten becomes one in a hundred, and one half becomes one quarter. At low Mek, p squared stays tiny, then climbs steeply.
scenes.caption: ERK shuts off completely. Removing either phosphate silences it, because ERK requires both to align its active site. In the test tube, if one hit has chance p, two independent hits have chance p squared. So one in ten becomes one in a hundred, and one half becomes one quarter. At low MEK, p squared stays tiny, then climbs steeply.
scenes.visual: The crimson phosphatase clips off 'Tyr-P'; immediately violet ERK dims completely to resting slate even though 'Thr-P' remains. Beside the cell, a clean computed curve compares '1-site (p)' (straight diagonal) with '2-site independent (p squared)' (flat at low input, rising steeply), then briefly adds a dashed note 'Schematic: in some cells, less steep'. Empathy fix: Beside the curves, write the worked pair as spoken: 'p = 0.1 → p² = 0.01' then 'p = 0.5 → p² = 0.25'. The crowding caveat is now an on-screen footnote only: 'In some cells, crowding may make this nearly one step'.
scenes.narration: ERK shuts off completely. Removing either phosphate silences it, because ERK requires both to align its active site. In the test tube, if one hit has chance p, two independent hits have chance p squared. So one in ten becomes one in a hundred, and one half becomes one quarter. At low MEK, p squared stays tiny, then climbs steeply.

scenes.tts: Three kinases in series do more than carry a message. Each tier can amplify the signal, sharpen its rise, and open control points for phosphatases and feedback. Mek is a narrow pipe aimed almost only at Erk. Active Erk then fans out widely across cytoplasm and nucleus.
scenes.caption: Three kinases in series do more than carry a message. Each tier can amplify the signal, sharpen its rise, and open control points for phosphatases and feedback. MEK is a narrow pipe aimed almost only at ERK. Active ERK then fans out widely across cytoplasm and nucleus.
scenes.visual: Return to the full cell cross-section. Glowing emerald Raf activates several blue MEK blocks; blue MEK funnels through a sleek narrow channel labelled 'Narrow pipe' solely onto violet ERK. Doubly phosphorylated violet ERK bursts outward along branching arrows ('Wide fan') to cytoplasmic protein blocks and downward into the indigo nucleus.
scenes.narration: Three kinases in series do more than carry a message. Each tier can amplify the signal, sharpen its rise, and open control points for phosphatases and feedback. MEK is a narrow pipe aimed almost only at ERK. Active ERK then fans out widely across cytoplasm and nucleus.

scenes.tts: In the nucleus, Erk phosphorylates Elk one, which helps switch on c fos. That is an immediate early gene, one of the first genes on, within minutes.
scenes.caption: In the nucleus, ERK phosphorylates Elk-1, which helps switch on c-fos. That is an immediate early gene, one of the first genes on, within minutes.
scenes.visual: Inside the indigo nucleus, violet ERK stamps a gold 'P' onto 'Elk-1', lighting up a gene bar labelled 'c-fos'. In the cytosol beside Raf–MEK–ERK, two muted three-block lanes labelled 'JNK pathway' and 'p38 pathway' slide into view. A cyan bracket labelled 'Scaffold (KSR)' clamps emerald Raf, blue MEK, and violet ERK neatly together so arrows stay in their own lane. Empathy fix: Add 'Immediate early genes = first genes on, within minutes'. JNK, p38 and scaffolds are now on screen only, as small labels: 'Parallel stress cascades: JNK, p38' and 'Scaffolds hold each module together'.
scenes.narration: In the nucleus, ERK phosphorylates Elk-1, which helps switch on c-fos. That is an immediate early gene, one of the first genes on, within minutes.

scenes.tts: So this three-tier relay is no wasteful detour. Ras gripping Raf starts the chain at the membrane. Three kinases in series can then amplify, sharpen, and control that signal. Finally, Erk fans out to proteins and genes.
scenes.caption: So this three-tier relay is no wasteful detour. Ras gripping Raf starts the chain at the membrane. Three kinases in series can then amplify, sharpen, and control that signal. Finally, ERK fans out to proteins and genes.
scenes.visual: Full cell cross-section glows steadily from top to bottom: gold receptor, coral Ras-GTP gripping paired emerald Raf, blue MEK narrow pipe, cyan scaffold, and violet ERK fanning to cytoplasm and nucleus, smoothly pulsing in sequence.
scenes.narration: So this three-tier relay is no wasteful detour. Ras gripping Raf starts the chain at the membrane. Three kinases in series can then amplify, sharpen, and control that signal. Finally, ERK fans out to proteins and genes.

scenes.visual: Clean dark-navy end card displaying one white line centered (size 36), with no subtitle below it: 'A three-kinase relay can amplify, sharpen, and control a membrane signal.'
